- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 30d high), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought signals.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is neutral (0.27–0.53); forecast should align with 14-day moving average if sentiment <0.5.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term downward drift; if sentiment is negative or flat, subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast baseline.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model delays correction; forecast should adjust 2–3 days ahead of sentiment shift to avoid lag.
